statement: For an original based ambient-null plane centralizer loop, let W be an operator-invariant union of its open generated-group orbits whose full local centralizers have dimension one and whose frontier points are fixed by the generated group. The loop equal to the original loop on W and the identity outside W has an actual global based null-homotopy in the original operator centralizer. The induced principal-base contraction is the median of the original real lift. Both maps and inverses are jointly continuous across arbitrary accumulation of open orbits. The theorem retains all original source covers, deck labels and stabilizer restriction kernels, and includes empty global nonopen-target families.
depends_on: C27 real median contraction and naturality; C30 proper full local centralizer and exact operator restriction; C32 ambient-null restriction and closed original source lifts; C33 actual principal bundle and all-component affine fiber gauges; C62 actual word triangle and compact labelled-family interval control; the proved interlaced interval-selection construction
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), infinite-operator zero-level comparison and controlled moving-base extension at fixed frontiers
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The proof constructs the actual principal quotient and the based isomorphism with every original source cover, retains all deck equations, and works in a complete compatible topology controlling global maps and inverses and all countably many source lifts. The continuous selection is proved by explicit successive partition-of-unity approximations, rather than inferred from the original prefix hulls.
notes: Successively tiny compact original increment families give a uniformly convergent infinite-product family in the exact closed compatible group of global maps and original lifts. Its compact parameter product supplies paths with their original labels. The nonconstant inverse evaluation of the real base path makes every sufficiently short increment family move any base point to both sides. Convex hulls of finite-product crossings therefore satisfy an interlaced lower-limit inclusion. Relative partition-of-unity approximations in the actual affine line bundle converge into the closed compact-family hull and attain the four prescribed endpoint faces exactly. The line-bundle transition retains negative fiber coefficients and every operator component. The resulting skew translations are actual intrinsic homeomorphisms with continuous inverse. C62 puts each selected value in one compact global three-family word image; inverse bracketing gives the corresponding inverse-family image. Every map in these compact families fixes the original fixed frontier, so both families paste continuously over every mixed-orbit accumulation. Conjugation over operator orbits is independent of the representative because the intrinsic maps commute with the full local centralizer. This proves the fixed-frontier moving-base extension. Selection of prescribed values on nonfixed frontier orbits, and residual zero-dimensional full local centralizer cases, remain unresolved in C12.
